year.evidence: Register 1784 keys to the SPANISH ROOT concession. Register (era 'spanish') and Hoffman simply pick different links of the same chain; 1784 is corroborated but approximate.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE No. 136 A / NORTHERN DISTRICT / LAS ANIMAS GRANT / JOSE MARIA SANCHEZ CLAIMANT'; transcript title page (PDF p3, stamped PAGE 1): 'for the place named "Las Animas"'. The file shows the rancho's double identity: Exhibit B translation caption (PDF p76, transcript p72) 'Rancho de las Las Animas granted under the name of Sitio de La Brea to Mariano de Castro, 1802'; Hoffman's 'Las Animas or Sitio de la Brea' agrees.

year.evidence: The file dates the viceregal concession to 1802, not 1803. Exhibit B (sworn translation of the expediente), caption at PDF p76 (transcript p72): 'Rancho de las Las Animas granted under the name of Sitio de La Brea to Mariano de Castro, 1802'. Translated summary of the expediente, PDF p78 (transcript p74): 'On the 5th day of July of 1802 Mariano Castro who was in Mexico presented to the Viceroy a petition praying for the tract of La Brea which was referred to the Royal Tribunal of accounts ... In pursuance of which the Viceroy granted his permission to Mariano Castro in order that he could go & establish himself & family on the tract called de la Brea, in which establishment no obstruction should be made under any pretext'. The claim petition, PDF p9 (transcript p5), states the same year with a day: 'That on the 17th day of August A.D. 1802, Felix Berenguer de Marquina Viceroy Governor &c of New Spain ... granted to Mariano Castro a tract of land known as La Brea.' Hoffman's 1802 agrees with the case file against the register.

governor.evidence: Right man, wrong spelling. The document itself (Spanish testimonio, PDF p30, transcript p26) reads: 'D. Felix Berenguer de Marquina, Teniente General de la Real Armada, Virrey Gobernador y Capitan General de las Provincias de Nueva España, Presidente de su Real Audiencia, Superintendente General de Real Hacienda...'; the translation names him again at PDF p79 (transcript p75), 'as ordered by the Viceroy Don Felix Berenguer de Marquina'. The register's 'Marquinas' (also Hoffman's printed form) carries a spurious final s; the surname is Marquina. Note also that he was Viceroy of New Spain, not a governor of California; the California governor at the time of the 1808 Las Animas/Carnadero relocation was Jose Joaquin de Arrillaga (PDF p101, transcript p101; PDF p77, transcript p73).

grantee.evidence: Exhibit B caption, PDF p76 (transcript p72): 'granted under the name of Sitio de La Brea to Mariano de Castro'; translated expediente summary, PDF p78 (transcript p74): 'the Viceroy granted his permission to Mariano Castro in order that he could go & establish himself & family on the tract called de la Brea'. Register 'Mariano Castro' correct; Jose Maria Sanchez, the red-label claimant, is a later purchaser (deeds from Josefa Romero 13 Dec 1850 and Carmen Castro 21 Sept 1850, PDF p134 and p137, transcript p127 and p129), NOT the grantee. The register did not fall into the claimant-for-grantee trap here.

notes: Two-stage title, which is why the dates in circulation disagree: (1) Viceroy Marquina's 1802 concession of the sitio de La Brea to Mariano Castro; (2) Castro was blocked by Mission San Juan Bautista's opposition and in Nov 1808 was ordered to relocate, selecting El Carnadero or Las Animas in lieu of La Brea (petition, PDF p9-p11, transcript p5-p7); (3) Governor Figueroa decreed a revalidation of the title on 7 Aug 1835 on the petition of Carlos Castro for the widow Maria Josefa Romero (translated index, PDF p82, transcript p77: 'Decree of the Political Chief. Monterey August 7th 1835'; the certified testimonio is dated Monterey 22 Aug 1835, PDF p74, transcript p70). A statement in Carlos Castro's petition, PDF p77 (transcript p73), that the tract was granted 'during the time of the Viceroy Iturrigaray about the year 1801' is an 1835 attorney's recollection and is wrong on both viceroy and year; it is not the decree and should not be used. VOLUME B (cubanc_lcf_nd136B.pdf) NOT READ: any re-reader wanting the District Court decree must open it.

name.evidence: Right rancho, misspelled. PDF p1 red label: 'CASE No. 345 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / ARROYO de la LAGUNA GRANT / JAMES & SQUIRE WILLIAMS CLAIMANT'; transcript title page (PDF p5, PAGE 1) 'for the place named "Arroyo de la Laguna"'; expediente cover in Spanish (PDF p35, PAGE 30) 'Espediente promovido por el C. Gil Sanchez en pretencion del parage llamado Arroyo de la Laguna'; Board transmittal letter (PDF p140, PAGE 130) 'for the place known by the name of Arroyo de la Laguna'. The register's 'Arroya De La Laguna' has an erroneous final a.

year.evidence: REGISTER IS RIGHT AND HOFFMAN IS WRONG. The grant decree, in the sworn translation of the expediente (PDF p46, PAGE 40): 'Monterey Feb. 20, 1839. Having seen the petition with this Record of Proceedings, containing the information of the Most Illustrious Ayuntamiento of Monterey, that of the administrador of Sta Cruz, with all the rest that has been presented & finding it be proper in conformity with the laws and regulations in regard to the matter, Don Gil Sanchez is declared owner in fee of the land known by the name of the Arroyo de la Laguna taking for its boundaries from the Arroyo de San Vicente as far as that of the Laguna as is shown in the design ... Thus I the Citizen Juan B. Alvarado Governor ad interim of the Californias have decreed ordered and signed. Alvarado.' The 1840 date in Hoffman and in the claimants' petition is the later confirmatory testimonio, and the file says so in terms (PDF p48, PAGE 42): 'Monterey 12 June 1840. In view of the approbation granted on the 19th day of May last past by the Most Excellent Departmental Assembly. Let a testimony of it be delivered to Don Gil Sanchez in confirmation of the land named Arroyo de la Laguna WHICH HE OBTAINED ON THE 20th OF FEB OF THE YEAR LAST PAST. The Sen Don Juan B. Alvarado Constitutional Gov of the Department of the Californias provided & signed it to which I certify. Alvarado.'

governor.evidence: Alvarado signed both the 20 Feb 1839 grant decree and the 12 June 1840 confirmatory testimonio: 'Thus I the Citizen Juan B. Alvarado Governor ad interim of the Californias have decreed ordered and signed. Alvarado.' (PDF p46-47, PAGE 40-41); Spanish original at PDF p39 (PAGE 34): 'Asi yo el Cno. Juan B. Alvarado Gobernador interino de las Californias lo decrete, mande y firme. Alvarado.' Register 'Alvarado' correct.

grantee.evidence: Grant decree, PDF p46 (PAGE 40): 'Don Gil Sanchez is declared owner in fee of the land known by the name of the Arroyo de la Laguna'. Register 'Gil Sanchez' correct. The red-label claimants James and Squire Williams are downstream purchasers: Gil Sanchez conveyed to James G. T. Dunleavy 30 July 1847 (deed, PDF p49, PAGE 43) and Dunleavy to the Williams brothers 21 Aug 1847 (petition, PDF p11, PAGE 6). The register did not confuse claimant with grantee.

Thompson delivered the Opinion of the Board confirming the claim (Vide page 65 of this Transcript.)' The claim carried through to final survey under the District Court docket: 'Certificate of U.S. Surveyor General that plat of survey & descriptive notes have been transmitted to Washington ... notes: Hoffman year flag RESOLVED IN THE REGISTER'S FAVOUR: two dates exist and the file distinguishes them explicitly. 20 Feb 1839 = Alvarado's grant decree declaring Gil Sanchez owner in fee; 12 June 1840 = the confirmatory testimonio issued after the Departmental Assembly's approval of 19 May 1840, which itself recites that Sanchez 'obtained' the land on 20 Feb of the previous year. The claimants' own petition and amended petition (PDF p11-12, PAGE 6-7) give 12 June 1840, which is probably Hoffman's source. A further layer: the Junta's committee on agriculture, art. 1 (PDF p47, PAGE 41), approved 'the Concession made by Sen Don Nicolas Gutierrez Superior Political Chief ad interim of the Department of the place called Arroyo de la Laguna in the person of Don Gil Sanchez', i.e. an antecedent 1836 concession under Gutierrez on Sanchez's petition of 14 Oct 1836 (PDF p43, PAGE 37); the operative grant to the named grantee is nonetheless Alvarado's of 20 Feb 1839. Hoffman's rancho column ('1 square league') is a size, not a name, which explains the name-mismatch flag.

grantee.evidence: THE REGISTER RECORDS THE U.S.-ERA CLAIMANT, NOT THE MEXICAN GRANTEE. The grant decree (PDF p14, PAGE 9) declares 'á D. Guillermo Dickey mejicano por naturalizacion dueño en propiedad de un parage situado en el Rio de Sacramento'; the title itself (PDF p15, PAGE 10) recites 'Por cuanto D. Guillermo Dickey mejicano por naturalizacion ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia cinco sitios de ganado mayor, entre las margenes del Rio Sacramento ... he venido en concederle provisionalmente dho. terreno'; the expediente cover is headed '1844. Espediente promovido por D. Guillermo Dickey en solicitud del terreno que se espresa' (PDF p10, PAGE 5). Bidwell's own petition says so plainly (PDF p9, PAGE 4): 'That on the 18th Nov. 1844 a grant of five leagues was made with a provisional title to William Dickey by Gov. Micheltorena ... that said grant was sold and conveyed to Geo. McKinstry Jr. by deed dated 7th May 1849 who conveyed one undivided half thereof to your Petitioner by deed dated July 4th 1849'. The District Court index lists the chain: 'Deed Dickey to McKinstry / Deed McKinstry to Bidwell / Dickey to Bidwell - derivation of title to Bidwell' (PDF p138, PAGE 123). Hoffman's 'William Dickey' agrees with the case file against the register.

outcome.evidence: The register's bare 'Confirmed' conceals a rejection. The Land Commission REJECTED this claim: 'San Francisco Feby 27 1855. In the same case Commissioner R. Aug. Thompson delivered the Opinion of the Board rejecting the claim (Vide page 31 of this Transcript)' (PDF p7, PAGE 3). Volume A then runs on through District Court testimony as late as 30 Dec 1859, filed 5 Jan 1860 (deposition of Alfred J. Amick for the United States, PDF p238-240, PAGE 230-233), and contains NO decree of confirmation. Any confirmation is a District Court decree lying in cubanc_lcf_nd199B.pdf, which was not read. Hoffman 1862 records the claim as confirmed and the register records a patent in 1865, so the District Court evidently reversed the Board, but that decree is not verified here.

notes: Grant of eleven sitios de ganado mayor on the Sierra Nevada foothills between the Cosumnes and Mokelumne rivers. The contested issue at the Commission was non-occupation: Ygnacio del Valle and Antonio F. Coronel were examined at length on the Mexican custom of denouncement for failure to take possession (PDF p11-16, PAGE 7-12), and Salvador Vallejo testified that occupation between 1840 and 1846 would have been impossible because of Indian resistance (PDF p9-10, PAGE 5-6). That is why the Board rejected. Salvador Vallejo's own dating of the grant to 1840 (PDF p9, PAGE 5) is witness testimony and was not relied on; the decree and expediente carry the grade. VOLUME B (cubanc_lcf_nd199B.pdf) NOT READ: a re-reader wanting the District Court decree, the survey, or the 1865 patent to Moss, Carpentier, Beale and Wohler must open it.
